title: Lost In Del Valle by Ned Van Zandt at Soho Playhouse #lostindelvalle ...
transcript: When a washed-up actor winds up in prison on a drug charge, being recognized by other inmates and enlisted for acting lessons is the last thing he expects. This was the case for Ned Van Zandt, whose solo show combines the material of a crime thriller with the stark yet cozy delivery of a campfire story. The production is simple but effective, letting the story speak for itself. With a crazy cast of over a dozen characters, we get a window into the most exciting yet harrowing eras of Ned's life. While it's overall a hopeful piece, it is a story of addiction and losing oneself, and I left thinking about the bittersweet nature of getting out of the woods, leaving behind the people who knew you and saw you at the lowest points in your life. As an actor, however, Ned is well-equipped to honor and immortalize those people, and this show is a great example of that. With that, another program for my collection.
